title: DR1 picks the transporter from one directory holding commercial and private transporters together and asks commercial-or-private only when adding a new one; the frontend asks commercial-or-private first and then shows a commercial-only list or a blank private form.

finding.frontend: The transporter section opens with "What type of transporter will move the animals?" and two radios — Commercial, hinted "A business approved to transport animals — you will choose one from a list", and Private, hinted "You or another individual moving the animals — you will give their address" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/copy/copy.en.js:78-87). The answer routes the user to one of two pages that offer no way back to the other and no way to add anything: a commercial-only pick list, or an empty private-transporter form (obligations/sections/transport.js:33-62 makes the two mutually exclusive, purging the commercial answer when the type flips to Private and the reverse). A private transporter the user has used before must be typed in again, and a commercial one can never be typed in at all.
finding.prototype: The section opens on the directory itself — "Transporter details", then "Select a transporter" over one table that mixes Commercial and Private rows and marks which is which in a Type column (app/views/transporter.html:113-153). The user picks a row. The type question exists only behind the "Add a transporter" button, where its heading is "Choose a transporter type" under the caption "Add a new transporter", it is preceded by the warning "Before you add this transporter, please ensure you have already searched for it first", it lists Private transporter before Commercial, and its Commercial option carries an entirely different meaning: "This can only be a commercial transporter from Northern Ireland".
finding.difference: Move the transporter section's entry from the type question to the directory, and make the directory hold private transporters as well as commercial ones. The type question becomes a step inside the add journey, reworded to DR1's heading and hints and with Private listed first. Everything a user does today stays reachable — choosing from the commercial list becomes choosing a Commercial row, and entering a private transporter becomes adding one — but both now start from the list. Do this before the add-a-commercial-transporter finding, which hangs off the same button.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding a private transporter listed anywhere on fe-transporter-commercial, or a route that reaches the frontend's transporter list without first answering the type question — the transporters-select page is reached only from the type page and its list is the fixed commercial record set.
finding.verification: Read all three screens' rendered DOM and screenshots, the frontend's transporters.njk, copy.en.js, records.js and obligations/sections/transport.js, and DR1's transporter.html, transporter-add.html and app/data/transporters.js. Ran the falsifier both ways: the frontend's commercial list holds only the two records from records.js, both commercial, and transporters-select is reached only from the type page, so it does not fire. Checked DR1's claim to mix the two types rather than taking it from the Type column alone: app/data/transporters.js types Aberdeen Livestock Ltd, Romanian Agri Exports SRL, Slovak Farm Export and Finnish Livestock Oy as Private and the other four as Commercial, and all eight are in the one table. The add page's caption, heading, warning text, option order and the Commercial hint are verbatim in the captured DOM and screenshot, and both sides' type field is named transporterType, so the named control crops on both. Citations resolve — transporters.njk:23-48 is the whole govukRadios block and transporter-add.html:30-52 is the caption, heading, warning and form opening. CORRECT on substance; one word narrowed, see correction.
finding.correction: Overstated wording, corrected because it made a claim about the journey rather than the page. finding.frontend said the type answer "routes the user to one of two dead-ended pages". True: neither page links to the other and neither offers an add control, which is what the finding means, but both continue the journey normally — the commercial pick list and the private form each post to kit.nextTarget and carry Save and continue. Checked by reading transporters-select.controller.js and private-transporter-details.controller.js and by looking at both captured screens, which show the Save and continue button. Reworded to say what is actually closed off. The same sentence's parenthesis now also says what obligations/sections/transport.js:33-62 does, which is purge the other answer on a type flip.

relatedTo.why: the add journey hangs off the directory this finding introduces
